persona: Priya, 29, a product manager who has an offer from a startup and has been circling the same argument with herself for weeks. Half of her wants the excitement, half suspects she's just bored, not stuck.

session.title: take the offer at the startup
options: Take the offer at the startup

notes.hope: to feel excited about work again, not dread Mondays
notes.worry: That the startup's growth is just noise, not real, and I'm about to trade security for hype.

persona: Daniel, 34, whose parents are aging two states away. Every call from home lands like an accusation, and he's treating 'move back' as the only responsible answer without examining it.

session.title: move back home to be near my parents

notes.hope: to stop feeling guilty every time my phone rings
notes.worry: That moving won't actually fix the guilt, and I'll have given up my career for nothing.

persona: Marisol, 27, deciding between a fully-funded PhD and staying in a job she's outgrown. She's tired of people telling her 'it's just five years' as if that settles anything.

session.title: start the PhD
options: Stay in my job and look for a raise elsewhere

notes.hope: to be doing research that actually matters instead of assisting someone else's
notes.worry: That five years from now I'll have a PhD and still no job in academia.

persona: Aisha, 31, six years into a relationship, crying on both sides of the question with no single reason she can point to. She can't tell if she's looking for a way out or just scared of staying.

notes.hope: to stop feeling numb around him
notes.worry: That I'm looking for a reason to leave instead of actually knowing if I want to.

persona: Ken, 36, married with one kid, anxious that renting means 'throwing money away' mostly because everyone around him says so. He and his wife have never actually run the numbers.

notes.hope: to stop feeling like we're behind everyone else our age
notes.worry: That we buy at the wrong time and end up house-poor.

persona: Ola, 41, three kids and a mortgage, quietly guilty for even wanting to quit a stable job to start her own business. She treats 'responsible' and 'quit' as opposites.

session.title: quit my job to start my own business

persona: Tom, 58, has been running retirement numbers for months. He isn't conflicted about the decision, just scared to finally say it out loud.
Jae, 33, offered a two-year expat assignment. Excited and scared in roughly equal measure, and aware he's deciding on almost no real information.

session.title: take the two-year assignment in Singapore

notes.hope: to prove to myself I can do something big
notes.worry: That I'll resent giving this up if I don't take it, but also that it wrecks my relationship.

persona: Sam, 30, single, remote-eligible, flip-flopping between two unfamiliar cities and a third option nobody's mentioned out loud: just staying put in Chicago.

session.title: move to Denver, move to Austin, or stay in Chicago

persona: Priyanka, 38, offered a promotion that requires relocating. Torn between her own ambition and her kids' stability, which no criterion on a standard list quite captures.

session.title: take the relocation for the promotion

notes.hope: to prove I can do this without sacrificing my kids
notes.worry: That the move works for my career and ruins things for them.

persona: Linh, 44, nineteen years married, quietly building a case against her husband in her head for months without ever actually testing whether he'd change.

notes.hope: to feel like myself again, not disappearing into this marriage
notes.worry: That I've already decided and I'm just building the case.
